summary:
Over the past few weeks, I’ve been talking with engineers across the organization to better understand how they are using AI in their day-to-day work.

The goal wasn’t to measure adoption or create a scorecard. Instead, I wanted to learn what people are actually doing, what is working well, where they see value, and what is getting in the way.

These conversations helped surface real use cases, common patterns, and opportunities to improve and was a lot about the human behind the process of using AI. 

In this session, I’ll share the approach I took, the questions I asked, the key insights that emerged, and some ideas for actions we could take next, from sharing best practices to investing in tools, workflows, and convictions
title: 20+ Interviews About AI Usage by Engineers: Questions, Learnings, Fears, and the Human Side of AI

summary:
Almost 2 years ago, the Time team set out to keep absences, schedules, time tracking, and their payroll impact consistent across systems. We reached for event sourcing. It was a sound choice. So how did we end up with a system that worked, but was buried under complexity that had nothing to do with the actual problem?

This is a retrospective on how a well-intentioned architecture quietly drifted. We will share the moment we realised why, and how we are climbing back out. Along the way we will name the trap we fell into, a concept called semantic diffusion. You will probably start spotting it in your own domains by the end.

No laptop and no prior event-sourcing knowledge needed. If you have ever inherited a system that felt far more complicated than the problem it solved, come along.
title: A Time Team Story - How Emmett Helped Us Find Our Way Back

summary:
Progress hasn't always meant a better life for the people living through it. The industrial revolution gave us extraordinary things, and also exhausted bodies, displaced workers, and decades of figuring out what had just happened. We're in one of those moments again.
Over the past year, working with AI has become more intense for most of us, and most of us have hit at least one point of feeling drained.
Our attention is pulled in too many directions at once: keeping up with the flood of news, running several things in parallel, spending hours reviewing AI output instead of building in a long focused flow, and sitting with bigger questions about the future of our jobs and even our society. The essence of the work is changing, from focusing on producing one thing at a time, to thinking, delegating, and reviewing several things. And it's tiring in a way we didn't sign up for.
It's still genuinely exciting to be part of this shift, and collectively we can do greater things than ever. But to get there without burning out, we need to step back and think about how to do this the right way, in a way we can sustain. Let's talk about it: a short intro from me, and most importantly, your insights. How do you organise your day with AI so it doesn't drain you? What exactly is draining?
title: AI Fatigue: our brains deserve a step back

summary:
Ghita and Margaux ran a research project on onboarding frictions using a stack of Dust agents, NotebookLM, and a Salesforce MCP to crunch 400+ data points from 7 sources (CES, support tickets, Copilot logs, Slack escalations, call transcripts...) in about 2 weeks.
This talk is a honest walkthrough of the whole thing: the pipeline we built, where AI actually saved us time and where it confidently hallucinated root causes. We'll also talk about the rework tax, why expert knowledge doesn't serialize into a prompt, and why AI workflows are weirdly optimized for solo mode.
Come if you're curious about what research looks like from the inside !
title: Behind the scenes of an AI-powered research project

summary:
PayFit Copilot isn't one assistant, it's a fleet of agents serving different personas: admins, employees, and our support teams. In this talk we crack open how it actually works in production, end to end.
We'll walk through the architecture and the stack we built on: the general agents that handle day-to-day questions, the specialized agents that take over for deeper work, the tools that let agents actually do things, and how Dora, our classification system, analyzes incoming queries to extract the topic and feed the right context into the agents that answer the questions.
room: LGA
We'll then get into the parts that make this stack livable: how we manage our prompts as versioned artifacts, how we iterate on them and promote them safely from dev to production, and how we evaluate agent quality so we know when a change actually improves things instead of just feeling like it does.
We'll touch briefly on observability, the traces and signals that let us debug a real conversation after the fact.
You'll leave with a concrete mental model of a multi-agent system running on real payroll dat: what works, where we bled, and what we'd do differently.
title: The Anatomy of PayFit Copilot: cracking open our AI stack

summary:
Generative AI is powerful, but tokens cost money and energy. This session explores practical strategies to use AI intelligently without burning your budget (and the world). We'll cover when to use AI, when to skip it, prompt optimization, and how to measure actual ROI from your AI investments. 
Bonus: being smart about tokens also means being responsible about energy consumption. Because the golden age of free tokens is over, and now we need to think.
title: Tokens aren't free: Smart AI usage today
